original_test_intent: At a controlled 25C reference environment, run 1,000 complete approved PCIe speed and intended lane-width retraining matrices on the selected AMD GPU link with verified readbacks, no new errors and final baseline restoration.
original_method: Resolve whether width16 readback belongs to every loop and define width acceptance; pin AGT, endpoint/upstream topology and 25C DUT sensor/tolerance/soak; preserve original link and error baseline; execute each approved transition with same-loop status/error readback, count only complete matrices, stop first anomaly and restore link/environment after exactly 1,000 successful loops.
manual_activity: PCIe/environment owner resolves width16 same-loop readback and width oracle, approves the 25C setup and 1,000-loop recovery plan, and owns verdict.
required_inputs: Signed AGT/hash and corrected option/value documentation
Stable GPU endpoint/upstream topology, capabilities and original state
Decision on step20 readback inclusion and per-width expectations
Dedicated maintenance, watchdog, telemetry, error parser and restore/OOB procedure
safety_requirements: Never accept width16 without attributable same-loop readback
Do not run malformed unresolved syntax
Verify link identity/state and errors after every transition
Abort on link loss, reset, AER/XID/log or power/thermal anomaly
Preserve baseline, stop-first-error and verify original link/environment restore
agent_execution_scope: Await loop/readback/oracle decision and validate all gates
Count only loops with complete same-loop evidence
Stop, restore and report without DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve repeated range and width16 readback placement
Approve corrected syntax, width expectations and 25C controls
Disposition partial/error loops and set PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: After decision, issue vendor-confirmed speed/width commands sequentially and capture status/error evidence immediately within the same loop; never associate the next loop's status with the prior width16 request.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: 25C, generations1..4, widths1/2/4/8/16 and 1,000 loops remain; step20 placement is pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use loop-scoped transaction IDs so every request/readback/error snapshot is paired before loop commit, with chamber trace and final restore.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates off-by-one evidence attribution created by the repeat boundary.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A width16 command without its own verified status cannot count as completed width16 coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some platforms may retrain to a supported value different from the request; approved expected negotiation is required per link capability.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row241 Wistron-AMD GPU-00234-V002: decide whether width16 status step20 is inside every one of the 1,000 loops despite literal repeat steps1..19; approve corrected AGT syntax, per-width expected negotiation/PASS rule absent from Criteria, and the 25C DUT sensor/tolerance/soak plus final restore contract.

review_improvement: Exposes the off-by-one width16 verification defect and mandates loop-scoped attribution instead of treating an unverified command as coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The last width command and its readback straddle the literal repeat boundary. A naïve loop can associate a later status with the wrong request or omit it entirely while still reporting 1,000 iterations. Transaction IDs and same-loop readback prevent this off-by-one false pass. The reference-temperature variant remains useful because it separates environmental effects from the hot/cold cases, but only if the DUT temperature and matrix are controlled identically.
